The research paper explores the recycling and reuse of polyethylene (PE) waste as antistatic and EMI shielding materials.
Conductive carbon black is used to improve the electrical conductivity of PE waste.
The electrical conductivity of neat PE is 6.78×10−18 S/cm.
The EMI shielding effectiveness of the 10 wt% carbon-loaded composite is 33 dB.
The solution mixing technique is used to recycle PE waste.
A full dispersion of carbon black is achieved after 40 min of sonication.
The electrical percolation threshold value is 3.5 wt% loading of carbon black.
The electrical conductivity increases with increasing carbon black loading within the polymer matrix.
The range of electrical conductivity for antistatic materials is between 10−12 S/cm to 10−8 S/cm.
The tensile properties of PE have reduced substantially after reprocessing.
The addition of carbon black has improved the strength of PE up to a certain loading.
The EMI shielding effectiveness of the composite system is measured using a Scalar Network Analyzer (HP 8757C).
The tensile properties are measured using a tensile testing instrument Instron (Model 3345).
The electrical conductivity is measured using a Keysight 34465A Truevolt 6½ digital multimeter.
The UV-VIS spectra are measured using a Spectro UV-VIS (Model UVD-3500).
The FTIR spectra are measured using a FTIR-8400 (SHIMADZU Precision Instruments, Inc.).
The DSC study is performed using a differential scanning calorimeter (Q1000, TA instruments).
The TGA analysis is performed using a thermogravimetric analyzer (PER NETZSCH TG 209 F3 Tarsus).
The SEM study is performed using a scanning electron microscope (SEM, model Supra 40, Carl Zeiss SMT AG).
